title: DROP: Poison Dilution via Knowledge Distillation for Federated Learning

C-a.quote: DROP introduces a novel architecture that combines effectively three key components: (1) Agglomerative Clustering to identify and separate anomalous updates, (2) Activity Monitoring to track and penalize suspicious clients over multiple rounds, and (3) Knowledge Distillation to cleanse the global model using a synthetic dataset guided by the consensus logits from benign client updates.
C-a.locator: §I; all three purposes are stated as defense in that sentence, and the distillation stage's purpose is restated at §IV, "impact of stealthy backdoor updates while preserving the model's utility for legitimate tasks". The stages are sequential within a round: Algorithm 1 runs clustering (§IV-A), then the penalty update, then distillation, and §IV-B states the dependency, "During each training round t, the clustering component (Section IV-A) determines whether a client's update is beni[gn]", with the penalty score updated "based on the clustering results from each round"

C-b.quote: complementing the clustering component, is an activity monitoring mechanism, which tracks the behavior of participating clients over the course of training. This mechanism addresses a limitation of clustering-based defenses in federated learning, which assume that the number of malicious updates in a round is smaller than the number of benign ones.
C-b.locator: §IV-B; the reason for pairing is that the second constituent covers a stated failure mode of the first, and the failure mode is named (per-round majority assumptions). The complementary-regime version is at §IV-A, "isolates malicious updates by clustering submitted models based on their pairwise Euclidean distances. This process is particularly effective against high-DPR attacks, where malicious updates deviate significantly from benign updates", which assigns the clustering stage a region of the attack space and leaves the stealthy low-DPR region to the other two stages

C-c.quote: Attack success is measured by the Attack Success Rate (ASR), while maintaining high Main Task Accuracy (MTA) ensures stealthiness.
C-c.locator: §III; the evidence for the composition is the assembled system's MTA and ASR, reported against seven existing defenses and three attacks (BadNets, Neurotoxin, Chameleon) across CIFAR-10, CINIC-10 and EMNIST and across data poisoning rates and malicious client ratios -- "Fig. 3: ASR (%) for our defense (DROP) and various existing defenses for 10 FL configurations (1.25% DPR, 20% MCR) where stealthy attacks are possible"

C-d.quote: Unlike DROP, DROPlet omits the knowledge distillation component and focuses solely on agglomerative clustering and activity monitoring to mitigate adversarial influences with minimal overhead.
C-d.locator: §VI; this is the paper's ONLY component-level variant and it removes the DOWNSTREAM stage while the upstream clustering and monitoring are held fixed, which is the direction the rubric declines. The word "ablation" does not occur in the paper (0 hits over 93836 characters) and no arm removes, substitutes or re-parameterizes clustering or monitoring. The grid search that does exist is over the CLIENT LEARNING CONFIGURATION, external to the defense: "we conduct a grid-search analysis over key hyperparameters, varying the client's learning rate, batch size, and number of epochs on the CIFAR-10 dataset" (§III)

C-e.quote: This reputation-based approach ensures robustness against per round benign-to-malicious client ratio fluctuations, where the proportion of malicious clients can vary widely across rounds due to random client selection.
C-e.locator: §IV-B; the claim states what one constituent contributes to the combined result. A second constituent-level attribution is at §IV-A, "This process is particularly effective against high-DPR attacks, where malicious updates deviate significantly from benign updates", and a third at §VI on the variant, "DROPlet offers robust protection by leveraging clustering to detect anomalies and activity monitoring to penalize malicious clients. However, it may not be effective against stealthy, low-DPR attacks"

coder_note:
THIS IS THE THIRD PRIMARY = YES, AND IT IS THE STRONGEST OF THE THREE AS EVIDENCE. Fedward (2307.00356) and BRFL (2310.13403) are the other two. DROP is a 2025 paper with public code, seven baseline defenses, three attacks, three datasets, a glossary, a threat model with a formal success definition, and an explicit grid search over learning configurations -- by every ordinary standard of empirical care it is the best-executed paper in the frame so far. It composes three defense stages, gives a real reason for the pairing, validates on the composed system's MTA and ASR, asserts what its constituents contribute, and NEVER varies an upstream stage against a fixed downstream one. That combination is the audit's whole point: the missing contrast is not a symptom of a careless paper, and A4 should make that explicit rather than letting a reader infer that outcome-gated attribution is a property of weak work.

THE C-d = NO TURNS ENTIRELY ON THE DIRECTION OF DROPlet, AND I CHECKED IT HARDER THAN ANY OTHER CODE IN THE FRAME BECAUSE IT DECIDES A PRIMARY. The pipeline is clustering -> activity monitoring -> knowledge distillation. DROPlet is DROP with the DISTILLATION removed, i.e. the downstream stage deleted and the upstream pair held fixed. The rubric's exclusion is exact on this: "A component-ablation or leave-one-out table is NOT C-d unless the downstream mechanism is held fixed and the upstream stage is the only thing varied; dropping a component changes the system, not the upstream input to a fixed component." DROPlet changes the system. It is the same direction as CrowdGuard's Table V, G2uardFL's Table 10 and MTD's topology-only versus aggregation-only arms, and the opposite direction from RKD's without-Clustering arm and LASA's Di versus Spar+Di, both of which coded YES. Rule 4's benefit of the doubt cannot rescue it either, because rule 4 forgives IMPERFECTION in an experiment that plausibly holds a downstream mechanism fixed while varying an upstream stage, and this experiment does the reverse; there is nothing to give the doubt to.

AND DROPlet IS REPORTED WITH FULL OUTCOMES, WHICH MAKES THE ROW SHARPER RATHER THAN WEAKER. The paper prints MTA and ASR for DROPlet beside DROP ("DROPlet achieves higher MTA than DROP and is robust in all cases, except for some extremely stealthy attacks (1.25% DPR, CIFAR-10)") and draws a constituent-level conclusion from the comparison. So this paper HAD the apparatus, the compute and the inclination to run a component contrast, ran one, and ran it in the direction that cannot identify the downstream stage's dependence on its input. The nearest miss in the frame.

WHAT WOULD HAVE MADE IT C-d = YES, stated so a reader can check the counterfactual: an arm holding the distillation stage fixed while feeding it the unclustered or unmonitored client set -- distillation-only versus clustering-then-distillation. DROPlet is the complement of that arm.

EXTRACTOR NOTE: every bucket underperformed on this paper. C-b returned 12 candidates and NONE was the complementing-the-clustering sentence; C-e returned 3, two of them hedged speculation about CIFAR-10's difficulty rather than constituent attribution; C-d returned 18 candidates, all baseline comparisons or learning-configuration statements. Both the coded C-b and the coded C-e came from targeted greps, and the C-d = NO was established by a negative search (zero hits for "ablation", zero for w/o-plus-component) plus reading §VI. This is the sixth C-d bucket shortfall and the first paper where three buckets missed simultaneously; A5 discloses it, because a coder trusting the aid on this paper could have coded C-b = NO and lost the primary.

THE C-b QUOTATION WAS REPAIRED AFTER CODING, AND THIS RECORD CARRIES A PRIMARY, SO THE DEFECT IS DISCLOSED HERE AS WELL AS IN THE LOG. The bracket "the number of malicious updates in a round is [below a threshold]" was my paraphrase; the paper says "smaller than the number of benign ones". Same claim, and the code does not move -- but the words are the evidence a reader re-adjudicates from, so the paraphrase was a defect of exactly the kind non-negotiable 5 forbids. C-d = NO, and therefore this row's primary status, never depended on that quotation. See results/literature_audit/quote_repair_log.md.
